items.question: Which is the drug of choice for absence (petit mal) seizures?
items.explanation: Ethosuximide (blocks T-type calcium channels) is first-line for absence seizures. Valproate is an alternative.

items.question: Which antidiabetic causes weight loss and has cardiovascular benefit?
items.explanation: SGLT2 inhibitors (empagliflozin) cause glucosuria, weight loss, and reduce cardiovascular and renal events.

items.question: Imatinib targets which tyrosine kinase?
items.explanation: Imatinib inhibits BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase in chronic myeloid leukaemia; also acts on c-KIT in GIST.

items.question: Which drug is used in hepatic encephalopathy to reduce ammonia?
items.explanation: Lactulose acidifies the colon, trapping ammonia as ammonium and promoting its excretion. Rifaximin is an add-on.

items.question: The document submitted to the regulator before first human testing is the?
items.explanation: The Investigational New Drug (IND) application, with preclinical data and protocol, is submitted before Phase I human studies.

whatsapp_text:
*PharmaCraft Daily - 13 Oct 2026*

🎓 *MBBS* (Central Nervous System)
Q: Which is the drug of choice for absence (petit mal) seizures?
Ans: Ethosuximide
Why: Ethosuximide (blocks T-type calcium channels) is first-line for absence seizures. Valproate is an alternative.

🩺 *NEET PG* (Endocrine)
Q: Which antidiabetic causes weight loss and has cardiovascular benefit?
Ans: Empagliflozin
Why: SGLT2 inhibitors (empagliflozin) cause glucosuria, weight loss, and reduce cardiovascular and renal events.

🏥 *INI-CET* (Anticancer)
Q: Imatinib targets which tyrosine kinase?
Ans: BCR-ABL
Why: Imatinib inhibits BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase in chronic myeloid leukaemia; also acts on c-KIT in GIST.

🌍 *FMGE* (Gastrointestinal)
Q: Which drug is used in hepatic encephalopathy to reduce ammonia?
Ans: Lactulose
Why: Lactulose acidifies the colon, trapping ammonia as ammonium and promoting its excretion. Rifaximin is an add-on.

🔬 *MD Pharmacology* (Drug Development)
Q: The document submitted to the regulator before first human testing is the?
Ans: IND
Why: The Investigational New Drug (IND) application, with preclinical data and protocol, is submitted before Phase I human studies.
